title: How to set up a simple daily pooja corner
excerpt: A calm corner needs only a few things done well.
content:
A daily pooja corner does not need a large space. Pick a quiet spot with natural light, keep a small shelf at chest height, and choose a few objects you will actually use every day: a diya, an incense holder and a small bell.

Clean brass once a week with lemon and salt. Keep a lined tray under the diya to catch oil, and store matches or a lighter in a closed box.

title: Caring for copper bottles and kalash
excerpt: Copper darkens with use. Here is how to keep it bright.
content:
Copper reacts with air and water and slowly darkens. This is normal and does not affect use. To restore the shine, rub the surface with half a lemon dipped in salt, rinse and dry immediately.

Avoid dishwashers and abrasive powders. Store bottles empty and open so moisture can escape.

title: Five ways to style a table runner
excerpt: Small textiles change a room faster than furniture.
content:
Lay it lengthwise for a classic look, across the table for a modern band, or fold it in half for a narrow console. A runner also works on a bed foot, a sideboard or a low bookshelf.

Pair block prints with plain ceramics so the pattern stays the focus.

title: Seasoning and using a cast iron tawa
excerpt: A well seasoned tawa gets better with every roti.
content:
Heat the tawa on a medium flame, wipe a thin layer of oil with a cloth and let it smoke lightly. Repeat three times before first use. After cooking, rinse with hot water, dry on the flame and apply a drop of oil.

Never soak cast iron and never use soap on a new tawa.
